body:
Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1987.

## Problem

handle_public_endpoints in bin/healer.sh treats state.unfixable[url] as permanent until that URL answers 2xx/3xx. The record is written when the backend is healthy and edge is in cooldown (the fault is outside the box). The short-circuit then skips the restart path on every later tick.

If the backend later dies, the URL stays non-2xx, so unfixable is never cleared, and the healer never restarts the now-unhealthy alloc. The public URL cannot come back on its own while that backend is down, so the outage sticks until a human restarts the alloc.

This is the #1952 unfixable contract, not introduced by #1955. The #1955 reminder now reports the backend as unhealthy, but it does not clear unfixable or restart the backend. Related, not the same bug: #1988 (restart cap), #1989 (false unfixable from another URL's cooldown).

## Expected

Once a recheck shows the backend is unhealthy or unregistered, drop unfixable for that URL and let the normal endpoint pass restart the backend alloc, subject to the existing cooldown and per-tick cap.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `bin/healer.sh` — `handle_public_endpoints`: the `state.unfixable[url]` record (written when the backend is healthy and edge is in cooldown) and the restart short-circuit that keeps it permanent; and the unfixable recheck/clear path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a recheck finds the backend behind an unfixable URL to be unhealthy or unregistered, `state.unfixable[url]` for that URL is dropped.
- [ ] After dropping unfixable, the normal endpoint pass proceeds to restart the backend alloc, respecting `HEALER_COOLDOWN_SECS` and the per-tick `HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS` cap.
- [ ] A URL recorded unfixable while its backend was healthy (during edge cooldown) is no longer stuck permanently once that backend later dies.
- [ ] A recheck finding the backend healthy (2xx/3xx) still clears unfixable as before.
- [ ] A regression test shows a backend that dies after its URL was marked unfixable now gets restarted.

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1987.

## Problem

`handle_public_endpoints` in `bin/healer.sh` records `unfixable` for a URL whenever that URL is still down, its backend is healthy, and the target job (`edge`) is in cooldown:

```bash
if in_cooldown "$target_job" "$now"; then
  if [ "$healthy" -eq 1 ]; then
    endpoint_down "$url" "$now"
  fi
```

Cooldown is per job, not per URL. An edge restart for `https://self.disinto.ai/forge/` (or any other edge restart still inside `HEALER_COOLDOWN_SECS`) makes a different down URL, such as `https://self.disinto.ai/ci/`, unfixable on the first tick its failure streak is high enough — without an endpoint restart for that URL. Once recorded, no further endpoint restart is attempted until the URL answers 2xx/3xx.

This predates #1987. That PR notifies the owner on the tick `unfixable` is recorded, so a cooldown borrowed from another URL now also pages the owner with the Cloudflare-tunnel text.

## Failure mode

A transient 502 on `/ci/` during the cooldown from a `/forge/` edge restart is declared outside the box. The healer will not restart edge for `/ci/`, and (#1955) will tell the owner to check `cloudflared`.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `bin/healer.sh` — `handle_public_endpoints`: the `in_cooldown "$target_job" "$now"` + `$healthy -eq 1` branch that records `unfixable` via `endpoint_down`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `unfixable` is no longer recorded for a URL merely because *another* URL's job is in cooldown — the cooldown must be tied to the specific URL's own fault/job.
- [ ] A down URL's `unfixable` is recorded only on that URL's own failure streak / own endpoint-restart cooldown, not on a sibling URL's edge restart.
- [ ] A transient failure during another URL's cooldown no longer pages the owner with the cloudflared/unfixable text for the innocent URL.
- [ ] The existing unfixable semantics for a URL's own sustained failure are preserved.
- [ ] A regression test: an innocent URL does not become unfixable while a sibling URL is in its own cooldown.

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1987.

## Problem

`bin/healer.sh` documents a hard cap of 3 allocation restarts per tick (`HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS`), shared by the service-reregister pass and the public-endpoint pass. In `handle_public_endpoints` the cap is enforced only when the backend is healthy:

```bash
if [ "$healthy" -eq 1 ] && [ "$RESTARTS" -ge "$HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS" ]; then
  continue
fi
```

An unhealthy backend falls through and calls `act_on_endpoint` anyway, then increments `RESTARTS`. After the service pass has already used the budget, one more unhealthy endpoint restart makes it 4. The cap was not added by #1987; that PR only moved the same condition so a capped URL is still noted for escalation.

## Failure mode

A tick that has already restarted 3 allocations can still restart a fourth (and further) unhealthy public-endpoint backend. That violates the per-tick restart budget #1950/#1952 rely on to avoid a restart storm.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `bin/healer.sh` — `handle_public_endpoints`: the `$RESTARTS -ge $HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS` cap check that currently only applies when `$healthy -eq 1`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The per-tick restart cap `HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS` is enforced for ALL public-endpoint restarts in `handle_public_endpoints`, including unhealthy backends — not only healthy ones.
- [ ] Once the budget is exhausted (service pass + endpoint pass), no further allocation restarts occur in the same tick, healthy or unhealthy backend alike.
- [ ] A capped URL is still noted for escalation (preserving #1987 behavior) without an extra restart being attempted.
- [ ] The shared restart budget is not exceeded by a single tick (total restarts per tick <= `HEALER_MAX_RESTARTS`).
- [ ] A regression test confirms a tick that already restarted 3 allocations does not restart a 4th unhealthy endpoint.
